title: 🚀 'NASA' Changes the 'Artemis 3' Plan — No Moon Landing, but a Test in Earth Orbit!
body: 🚀 'NASA' Changes the 'Artemis 3' Plan — No Moon Landing, but a Test in Earth Orbit!

The US space agency "NASA" has radically changed the plan for the "Artemis 3" mission: its astronauts will not land on the Moon's surface as planned, but the mission will be a crewed test in Earth orbit, targeting launch in June 2027 at the earliest, lasting about 14 days, with four astronauts aboard the "Orion" capsule launched by the "SLS" rocket from Kennedy Space Center, at an altitude of about 466 kilometers.

The new plan is a three-rocket campaign: first, "Blue Origin" launches the experimental lander "Blue Moon Mark 2" on the "New Glenn" rocket, staying in orbit for up to a full month. On day three, "Orion" docks with it and the crew boards it to test life-support and control systems for about two days. Then "SpaceX" launches the experimental "Starship", and on day eight "Orion" docks with it from the front for about two hours, without crew transfer, to test docking only.

The mission is commanded by Randy Bresnik, with pilot Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency, and mission specialists Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio. The reason for the change is that the two landers are not ready yet, and the safety committee warned of mission-level risks. The mission also benefits from a gentler return for the "Orion" capsule, at about 28,000 kilometers per hour instead of 40,000 in a lunar return, after its heat shield lost part of its carbon layer on the uncrewed "Artemis 1" flight.

The first crewed Moon landing is now the goal of the "Artemis 4" mission in early 2028 near the Moon's south pole, followed by "Artemis 5" in late 2028, while "Starship" targets an uncrewed lunar landing in late 2027, and "Blue Moon" in early 2028. The lander for "Artemis 4" is still undecided, while China targets a crewed Moon landing around 2030.
Simply put: "NASA" decided to test the two landers near Earth first, before sending astronauts to the Moon aboard them.
Would you rather the Moon mission be delayed and safe, or NASA rush the landing despite the risks?
